newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada oil stocks surge on strong commodity prices.
newsitem.headline: Canada oil stocks surge on strong commodity prices.

text.p: Stocks in the Canadian oil and gas sector enjoyed another banner day on Thursday as strong commodity prices sent investors on a buying spree.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's oil and gas index surged 35.75 points to 5,708.63. That compared to the exchange's key TSE 300 index, which fell about eight points to 5380.
Canadian oils have climbed 299.23 points in a month.
Several large cap firms, including Anderson Exploration, Poco Petroleums, Canadian Occidental Petroleum, Renaissance Energy and Gulf Canada Resources, climbed in active volumes today.

"There's an overall view that with the commodity prices, the oil companies are doing well. The third quarter is going to be, I think, absolutely spectacular for the producers," said Rob Robinson, analyst with ScotiaMcleod Inc.
Robinson said most producers appeared poised to achieve their projected cash flow next year if oil prices fell to US$19.50 a barrel.
West Texas Intermediate prices have averaged above US$22 a barrel in the third quarter and on Thursday closed at US$24.81, up US$0.75.
Natural gas prices, both in the United States and Canada, have also strengthened considerably in the last two weeks as cold weather hit various North American regions.
"In the market there are three key factors -- gas and oil prices and the overall equity market," he said. "You're getting three out of three that are hitting."
Robinson said much of the buying action has been in stocks with high liquidity because of the need among large financial institutions to buy big positions in order to gain exposure.

He said ScotiaMcleod is projecting the oil and gas index to hit 6,656 points by the end of 1997, a 20 percent jump from the current level. The forecast is in line with the industry consensus, he said.
The forecast is based on a cash flow multiple of six times, he said. "That's contigent upon a US$19.50 oil price and a C$1.60 (per thousand cubic feet average Canadian) gas price," he said.
